import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Chern's conjecture (affine geometry)

Chern's conjecture for affinely flat manifolds (1955) states that the Euler characteristic of a
compact affine manifold vanishes.

An *affine manifold* is a manifold with an atlas modelled on $\mathbb{R}^n$ whose transition maps
are locally affine. Equivalently, it is a smooth manifold whose tangent bundle carries a flat
*torsion-free* connection: the affine charts are exactly the coordinate systems in which such a
connection is the standard flat one. Torsion-freeness is essential: Smillie constructed closed
manifolds with non-zero Euler characteristic whose tangent bundles admit flat connections with
torsion.

The conjecture is trivial in odd dimensions (by Poincaré duality) and is known when the manifold
is $2$-dimensional (Benzécri, Milnor), complete (Kostant–Sullivan), or carries a parallel volume
form (Klingler). It is open in general.

This file defines the Euler characteristic of a topological space through its rational singular
homology, and affine manifolds through the groupoid of locally affine maps.

*References:*
- [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chern%27s_conjecture_%28affine_geometry%29)
- [Wikipedia, List of unsolved problems in mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)
- [Kl17] B. Klingler, *Chern's conjecture for special affine manifolds*, Ann. of Math. 186 (2017),
  69–95.
- [FZ17] H. Feng, W. Zhang, *Flat vector bundles and open coverings*,
  [arXiv:1603.07248](https://arxiv.org/abs/1603.07248)
-/
namespace ChernsConjectureAffineGeometry
open CategoryTheory AlgebraicTopology Filter Topology
open scoped Manifold ContDiff
universe u
section EulerCharacteristic

noncomputable def bettiNumber (X : Type u) [TopologicalSpace X] (k : ℕ) : ℕ :=
  Module.finrank ℚ
    (((singularHomologyFunctor (ModuleCat.{u} ℚ) k).obj (ModuleCat.of ℚ (ULift.{u} ℚ))).obj
      (TopCat.of X))
blocks.docstring:
The `k`-th Betti number of a topological space `X`: the dimension over $\mathbb{Q}$ of the
`k`-th singular homology group $H_k(X; \mathbb{Q})$ (the coefficient module `ℚ` is lifted to the
universe of `X`). It is `0` when this homology group is infinite-dimensional.

justification.closest_existing_considered: AlgebraicTopology.singularHomologyFunctor (used as the underlying primitive); no Betti-number or Euler-characteristic declaration exists in Mathlib or FormalConjecturesForMathlib (grepped for euler/Betti/singularHomology).
justification.name: ChernsConjectureAffineGeometry.bettiNumber
justification.why_needed: Mathlib has singular homology as a functor (`AlgebraicTopology.singularHomologyFunctor`) but no Betti numbers; this takes `Module.finrank ℚ` of the k-th rational singular homology of X.

blocks.name: bettiNumber
blocks.text:
/-- The `k`-th Betti number of a topological space `X`: the dimension over $\mathbb{Q}$ of the
`k`-th singular homology group $H_k(X; \mathbb{Q})$ (the coefficient module `ℚ` is lifted to the
universe of `X`). It is `0` when this homology group is infinite-dimensional. -/
noncomputable def bettiNumber (X : Type u) [TopologicalSpace X] (k : ℕ) : ℕ :=

blocks.code:
noncomputable def eulerCharacteristic (X : Type u) [TopologicalSpace X] : ℤ :=
  ∑ᶠ k : ℕ, (-1 : ℤ) ^ k * bettiNumber X k
blocks.docstring:
The Euler characteristic $\chi(X) = \sum_k (-1)^k \dim_{\mathbb{Q}} H_k(X; \mathbb{Q})$ of a
topological space `X`, as a finite sum over all `k`. For a compact manifold the Betti numbers are
finite and vanish above the dimension, so this is the usual Euler characteristic. (For a space
with infinitely many non-zero Betti numbers `finsum` returns `0`, but no such space occurs here.)

justification.closest_existing_considered: Only a combinatorial Euler characteristic-like notion in IncidenceAlgebra (unrelated); nothing topological.
justification.name: ChernsConjectureAffineGeometry.eulerCharacteristic
justification.why_needed: No Euler characteristic of a topological space exists in Mathlib or the repo; defined as ∑ᶠ k, (-1)^k * bettiNumber X k.

blocks.name: eulerCharacteristic
blocks.text:
/-- The Euler characteristic $\chi(X) = \sum_k (-1)^k \dim_{\mathbb{Q}} H_k(X; \mathbb{Q})$ of a

-/

blocks.code:
@[category test, AMS 55]
theorem bettiNumber_punit_zero : bettiNumber PUnit.{u + 1} 0 = 1 := by
  have e := (singularHomologyFunctorZeroOfTotallyDisconnectedSpace (ModuleCat.{u} ℚ)
    (ModuleCat.of ℚ (ULift.{u} ℚ)) (TopCat.of PUnit.{u + 1}) ≪≫
      ModuleCat.coprodIsoDirectSum _).toLinearEquiv
  rw [bettiNumber, e.finrank_eq]
  simp [Module.finrank_directSum]
blocks.docstring: The zeroth Betti number of a point is $1$.

    bettiNumber PUnit.{u + 1} k = 0 := by
  have := ModuleCat.subsingleton_of_isZero

theorem eulerCharacteristic_punit : eulerCharacteristic PUnit.{u + 1} = 1 := by
  rw [eulerCharacteristic,
    finsum_eq_single _ 0 fun k hk ↦ by simp [bettiNumber_punit_of_ne_zero hk]]
  simp [bettiNumber_punit_zero]

section AffineGroupoid
variable (E : Type*) [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace ℝ E]

blocks.code:
def affinePregroupoid : Pregroupoid E where
  property f u := ∀ x ∈ u, ∃ g : E →ᴬ[ℝ] E, f =ᶠ[𝓝 x] g
  comp {f g _ _} hf hg _ _ _ x hx := by
    obtain ⟨a, ha⟩ := hf x hx.1
    obtain ⟨b, hb⟩ := hg (f x) hx.2
    refine ⟨b.comp a, ?_⟩
    have hfc : ContinuousAt f x := a.continuous.continuousAt.congr ha.symm
    filter_upwards [ha, hfc.eventually hb] with y hy₁ hy₂
    simp [← hy₁, hy₂]
  id_mem x _ := ⟨ContinuousAffineMap.id ℝ E, Eventually.of_forall fun _ ↦ rfl⟩
  locality _ h x hx :=
    let ⟨_, _, hxv, hv⟩ := h x hx
    hv x ⟨hx, hxv⟩
  congr hu hfg hf x hx :=
    let ⟨a, ha⟩ := hf x hx
    ⟨a, (eventuallyEq_of_mem (hu.mem_nhds hx) hfg).trans ha⟩
blocks.docstring:
The pregroupoid of locally affine maps of a real normed space `E`: a map `f : E → E` has the
property on a set `u` if, near every point of `u`, it coincides with a continuous affine map
`E →ᴬ[ℝ] E`. When `E` is finite-dimensional every affine map is continuous, so this is the
usual notion of a locally affine map.

justification.closest_existing_considered: contDiffPregroupoid / conformalPregroupoid (same design pattern, different property); Mathlib has no affine groupoid, no connections, and no torsion.
justification.name: ChernsConjectureAffineGeometry.affinePregroupoid
justification.why_needed: Pregroupoid on a real normed space E with property `∀ x ∈ u, ∃ g : E →ᴬ[ℝ] E, f =ᶠ[𝓝 x] g` (locally affine maps); the comp/id/locality/congr axioms are proved.

blocks.docstring:
The groupoid of locally affine open partial homeomorphisms of a real normed space `E`.

A charted space `M` modelled on `E` with `HasGroupoid M (affineGroupoid E)` is an *affine
manifold*: the transition maps between any two charts of its atlas are locally affine.

justification.closest_existing_considered: contDiffGroupoid, conformalGroupoid, continuousGroupoid — none captures affine transition maps.
justification.name: ChernsConjectureAffineGeometry.affineGroupoid
justification.why_needed: `(affinePregroupoid E).groupoid`; `HasGroupoid M (affineGroupoid E)` is the affine-manifold condition. Accompanied by API: `affineGroupoid_le_contDiffGroupoid` and an instance `IsManifold 𝓘(ℝ, E) ∞ M` for affine manifolds.

blocks.name: affineGroupoid
blocks.text:
/-- The groupoid of locally affine open partial homeomorphisms of a real normed space `E`.

A charted space `M` modelled on `E` with `HasGroupoid M (affineGroupoid E)` is an *affine
manifold*: the transition maps between any two charts of its atlas are locally affine. -/
def affineGroupoid : StructureGroupoid E := (affinePregroupoid E).groupoid

blocks.code:
@[category API, AMS 53 57]
theorem affineGroupoid_le_contDiffGroupoid (n : WithTop ℕ∞) :
    affineGroupoid E ≤ contDiffGroupoid n 𝓘(ℝ, E) := by
  refine groupoid_of_pregroupoid_le _ _ fun f s hf ↦ ?_
  simp only [contDiffPregroupoid, modelWithCornersSelf_coe, modelWithCornersSelf_coe_symm,
    Function.comp_id, Function.id_comp, Set.preimage_id, Set.range_id, Set.inter_univ]
  intro x hx
  obtain ⟨a, ha⟩ := hf x hx
  exact (a.contDiff.contDiffAt.congr_of_eventuallyEq ha).contDiffWithinAt
blocks.docstring: Locally affine maps are smooth, so the affine groupoid is contained in every `C^n` groupoid.
blocks.name: affineGroupoid_le_contDiffGroupoid
blocks.text:
/-- Locally affine maps are smooth, so the affine groupoid is contained in every `C^n` groupoid. -/
@[category API, AMS 53 57]
theorem affineGroupoid_le_contDiffGroupoid (n : WithTop ℕ∞) :
    affineGroupoid E ≤ contDiffGroupoid n 𝓘(ℝ, E) := by
  refine groupoid_of_pregroupoid_le _ _ fun f s hf ↦ ?_
  simp only [contDiffPregroupoid, modelWithCornersSelf_coe, modelWithCornersSelf_coe_symm,
    Function.comp_id, Function.id_comp, Set.preimage_id, Set.range_id, Set.inter_univ]
  intro x hx
  obtain ⟨a, ha⟩ := hf x hx
  exact (a.contDiff.contDiffAt.congr_of_eventuallyEq ha).contDiffWithinAt

blocks.code:
@[category API, AMS 53 57]
instance IsManifold.of_hasGroupoid_affineGroupoid {M : Type*} [TopologicalSpace M]
    [ChartedSpace E M] [HasGroupoid M (affineGroupoid E)] : IsManifold 𝓘(ℝ, E) ∞ M :=
  IsManifold.mk' _ _ _
    (gr := hasGroupoid_of_le inferInstance (affineGroupoid_le_contDiffGroupoid E ∞))
blocks.docstring: An affine manifold is a smooth manifold.
blocks.name: IsManifold.of_hasGroupoid_affineGroupoid
blocks.text:
/-- An affine manifold is a smooth manifold. -/
@[category API, AMS 53 57]
instance IsManifold.of_hasGroupoid_affineGroupoid {M : Type*} [TopologicalSpace M]
    [ChartedSpace E M] [HasGroupoid M (affineGroupoid E)] : IsManifold 𝓘(ℝ, E) ∞ M :=
  IsManifold.mk' _ _ _
    (gr := hasGroupoid_of_le inferInstance (affineGroupoid_le_contDiffGroupoid E ∞))

@[category research open, AMS 53 57]
theorem cherns_conjecture_affine_geometry (n : ℕ) (hn : 0 < n) (M : Type*) [TopologicalSpace M]
    [T2Space M] [CompactSpace M] [ChartedSpace (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n)) M]
    [HasGroupoid M (affineGroupoid (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n)))] :
    eulerCharacteristic M = 0 := by
  sorry
blocks.docstring:
**Chern's conjecture (affine geometry).** Let $M$ be a compact affine manifold of dimension
$n \geq 1$, that is, a compact Hausdorff manifold with an atlas modelled on $\mathbb{R}^n$ whose
transition maps are locally affine (equivalently, a closed smooth manifold whose tangent bundle
carries a flat torsion-free connection). Then the Euler characteristic of $M$ vanishes:
$\chi(M) = 0$.

Here `M` is a compact Hausdorff space charted on all of $\mathbb{R}^n$, hence a closed manifold
(second countability follows from compactness, and smoothness from the affine atlas, see
`IsManifold.of_hasGroupoid_affineGroupoid`). `M` is not assumed connected or orientable, and
`eulerCharacteristic M` is the alternating sum of the rational Betti numbers of `M`. The
zero-dimensional case is excluded because a single point is a compact affine manifold with
$\chi = 1$ (see `eulerCharacteristic_punit`); for odd $n$ the statement is a consequence of
Poincaré duality.
blocks.name: cherns_conjecture_affine_geometry

/-- **Chern's conjecture (affine geometry).** Let $M$ be a compact affine manifold of dimension
$n \geq 1$, that is, a compact Hausdorff manifold with an atlas modelled on $\mathbb{R}^n$ whose
transition maps are locally affine (equivalently, a closed smooth manifold whose tangent bundle
carries a flat torsion-free connection). Then the Euler characteristic of $M$ vanishes:
$\chi(M) = 0$.

Here `M` is a compact Hausdorff space charted on all of $\mathbb{R}^n$, hence a closed manifold
(second countability follows from compactness, and smoothness from the affine atlas, see
`IsManifold.of_hasGroupoid_affineGroupoid`). `M` is not assumed connected or orientable, and
`eulerCharacteristic M` is the alternating sum of the rational Betti numbers of `M`. The
zero-dimensional case is excluded because a single point is a compact affine manifold with
$\chi = 1$ (see `eulerCharacteristic_punit`); for odd $n$ the statement is a consequence of
Poincaré duality. -/
@[category research open, AMS 53 57]
theorem cherns_conjecture_affine_geometry (n : ℕ) (hn : 0 < n) (M : Type*) [TopologicalSpace M]
    [T2Space M] [CompactSpace M] [ChartedSpace (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n)) M]
    [HasGroupoid M (affineGroupoid (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n)))] :
    eulerCharacteristic M = 0 := by
  sorry
end ChernsConjectureAffineGeometry

claims.decomposer_note: Single universally quantified Prop: for every compact (closed, boundaryless) smooth manifold M carrying an affine structure — i.e. a flat, torsion-free connection on TM, equivalently an atlas with affine transition maps — one has χ(M) = 0; torsion-freeness is essential (Smillie's counterexamples for merely flat tangent connections must not be admitted), the odd-dimensional case is trivial by Poincaré duality, and connectedness/orientability are not assumed; the article's proven special cases (dim 2, complete, parallel volume form) and the generalized aspherical/simplicial-volume conjectures are background, not questions posed by the statement.
claims.reviewer_why: c04 encodes an affine manifold as a ChartedSpace on EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n) with HasGroupoid M (affineGroupoid _), where affineGroupoid is the Pregroupoid.groupoid of maps that agree near every point with a (continuous) affine map — exactly the standard (Aff(ℝⁿ),ℝⁿ)-structure definition, which builds in torsion-freeness and excludes Smillie's flat-with-torsion examples. Compactness + T2 + charts on all of ℝⁿ give a closed manifold (second countability follows from compactness; smoothness is PROVED from the affine atlas as an API instance, checked to coincide with 𝓡 n). Euler characteristic is ∑ᶠ (-1)^k dim_ℚ H_k(X;ℚ) via Mathlib's singularHomologyFunctor, universe-polymorphic via ULift ℚ; finsum/finrank junk values are unreachable for compact smooth manifolds. Connectedness/orientability not assumed; odd n retained. `0 < n` is a necessary domain restriction (a point is a compact affine 0-manifold with χ=1, witnessed by the proved test eulerCharacteristic_punit); explained in the docstring. I verified the hypotheses are satisfiable (ℝⁿ itself has the affine groupoid) and that HasGroupoid/Pregroupoid.groupoid semantics in Mathlib match the intended 'transition map and inverse locally affine'. Edits: added docstrings to two test lemmas and expanded the main docstring (second countability, smoothness, Poincaré duality remark). c02/c06/c07 are equivalent but universe-0 only or with fewer tests; c03/c05/c08 are equivalent as a class of manifolds but use a less standard single-global-affine-map encoding and redundant IsManifold/Boundaryless hypotheses; c01 is provably false (no 0 < n, so PUnit is a counterexample).

Chern's conjecture states that the Euler characteristic of a compact affine manifold is zero.

decomposition_objections.text: None. The single-slot decomposition is appropriate. One remark: the table does not mention the dimension-0 degeneracy (a point is a compact affine manifold with χ = 1), so a hypothesis n ≥ 1 had to be added for the statement to be the intended one.

section EulerCharacteristic

/-- The `k`-th Betti number of a topological space `X`: the dimension over $\mathbb{Q}$ of the
`k`-th singular homology group $H_k(X; \mathbb{Q})$ (the coefficient module `ℚ` is lifted to the
universe of `X`). It is `0` when this homology group is infinite-dimensional. -/

  Module.finrank ℚ
    (((singularHomologyFunctor (ModuleCat.{u} ℚ) k).obj (ModuleCat.of ℚ (ULift.{u} ℚ))).obj
      (TopCat.of X))

/-- The Euler characteristic $\chi(X) = \sum_k (-1)^k \dim_{\mathbb{Q}} H_k(X; \mathbb{Q})$ of a
topological space `X`, as a finite sum over all `k`. For a compact manifold the Betti numbers are
finite and vanish above the dimension, so this is the usual Euler characteristic. (For a space
with infinitely many non-zero Betti numbers `finsum` returns `0`, but no such space occurs here.)
-/

  ∑ᶠ k : ℕ, (-1 : ℤ) ^ k * bettiNumber X k

/-- The zeroth Betti number of a point is $1$. -/
@[category test, AMS 55]
theorem bettiNumber_punit_zero : bettiNumber PUnit.{u + 1} 0 = 1 := by
  have e := (singularHomologyFunctorZeroOfTotallyDisconnectedSpace (ModuleCat.{u} ℚ)
    (ModuleCat.of ℚ (ULift.{u} ℚ)) (TopCat.of PUnit.{u + 1}) ≪≫
      ModuleCat.coprodIsoDirectSum _).toLinearEquiv
  rw [bettiNumber, e.finrank_eq]
  simp [Module.finrank_directSum]

/-- A point has no homology in positive degrees. -/
@[category test, AMS 55]
theorem bettiNumber_punit_of_ne_zero {k : ℕ} (hk : k ≠ 0) :
    bettiNumber PUnit.{u + 1} k = 0 := by
  have := ModuleCat.subsingleton_of_isZero
    (isZero_singularHomologyFunctor_of_totallyDisconnectedSpace (ModuleCat.{u} ℚ) k
      (ModuleCat.of ℚ (ULift.{u} ℚ)) (TopCat.of PUnit.{u + 1}) hk)
  exact Module.finrank_zero_of_subsingleton

/-- The Euler characteristic of a point is $1$. -/
@[category test, AMS 55]
theorem eulerCharacteristic_punit : eulerCharacteristic PUnit.{u + 1} = 1 := by
  rw [eulerCharacteristic,
    finsum_eq_single _ 0 fun k hk ↦ by simp [bettiNumber_punit_of_ne_zero hk]]
  simp [bettiNumber_punit_zero]

end EulerCharacteristic

variable (E : Type*) [NormedAddCommGroup E] [NormedSpace ℝ E]

/-- The pregroupoid of locally affine maps of a real normed space `E`: a map `f : E → E` has the

`E →ᴬ[ℝ] E`. When `E` is finite-dimensional every affine map is continuous, so this is the
usual notion of a locally affine map. -/
def affinePregroupoid : Pregroupoid E where
  property f u := ∀ x ∈ u, ∃ g : E →ᴬ[ℝ] E, f =ᶠ[𝓝 x] g
  comp {f g _ _} hf hg _ _ _ x hx := by
    obtain ⟨a, ha⟩ := hf x hx.1
    obtain ⟨b, hb⟩ := hg (f x) hx.2
    refine ⟨b.comp a, ?_⟩
    have hfc : ContinuousAt f x := a.continuous.continuousAt.congr ha.symm
    filter_upwards [ha, hfc.eventually hb] with y hy₁ hy₂
    simp [← hy₁, hy₂]
  id_mem x _ := ⟨ContinuousAffineMap.id ℝ E, Eventually.of_forall fun _ ↦ rfl⟩
  locality _ h x hx :=
    let ⟨_, _, hxv, hv⟩ := h x hx
    hv x ⟨hx, hxv⟩
  congr hu hfg hf x hx :=
    let ⟨a, ha⟩ := hf x hx
    ⟨a, (eventuallyEq_of_mem (hu.mem_nhds hx) hfg).trans ha⟩

/-- The groupoid of locally affine open partial homeomorphisms of a real normed space `E`.

A charted space `M` modelled on `E` with `HasGroupoid M (affineGroupoid E)` is an *affine
manifold*: the transition maps between any two charts of its atlas are locally affine. -/
def affineGroupoid : StructureGroupoid E := (affinePregroupoid E).groupoid

/-- Locally affine maps are smooth, so the affine groupoid is contained in every `C^n` groupoid. -/
@[category API, AMS 53 57]
theorem affineGroupoid_le_contDiffGroupoid (n : WithTop ℕ∞) :
    affineGroupoid E ≤ contDiffGroupoid n 𝓘(ℝ, E) := by
  refine groupoid_of_pregroupoid_le _ _ fun f s hf ↦ ?_
  simp only [contDiffPregroupoid, modelWithCornersSelf_coe, modelWithCornersSelf_coe_symm,
    Function.comp_id, Function.id_comp, Set.preimage_id, Set.range_id, Set.inter_univ]
  intro x hx
  obtain ⟨a, ha⟩ := hf x hx
  exact (a.contDiff.contDiffAt.congr_of_eventuallyEq ha).contDiffWithinAt

/-- An affine manifold is a smooth manifold. -/
@[category API, AMS 53 57]
instance IsManifold.of_hasGroupoid_affineGroupoid {M : Type*} [TopologicalSpace M]
    [ChartedSpace E M] [HasGroupoid M (affineGroupoid E)] : IsManifold 𝓘(ℝ, E) ∞ M :=
  IsManifold.mk' _ _ _
    (gr := hasGroupoid_of_le inferInstance (affineGroupoid_le_contDiffGroupoid E ∞))

end AffineGroupoid

/-- **Chern's conjecture (affine geometry).** Let $M$ be a compact affine manifold of dimension
$n \geq 1$, that is, a compact Hausdorff manifold with an atlas modelled on $\mathbb{R}^n$ whose
transition maps are locally affine (equivalently, a closed smooth manifold whose tangent bundle
carries a flat torsion-free connection). Then the Euler characteristic of $M$ vanishes:
$\chi(M) = 0$.

Here `M` is a compact Hausdorff space charted on all of $\mathbb{R}^n$, hence a closed manifold
(second countability follows from compactness, and smoothness from the affine atlas, see
`IsManifold.of_hasGroupoid_affineGroupoid`). `M` is not assumed connected or orientable, and
`eulerCharacteristic M` is the alternating sum of the rational Betti numbers of `M`. The
zero-dimensional case is excluded because a single point is a compact affine manifold with
$\chi = 1$ (see `eulerCharacteristic_punit`); for odd $n$ the statement is a consequence of
Poincaré duality. -/
@[category research open, AMS 53 57]
theorem cherns_conjecture_affine_geometry (n : ℕ) (hn : 0 < n) (M : Type*) [TopologicalSpace M]
    [T2Space M] [CompactSpace M] [ChartedSpace (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n)) M]
    [HasGroupoid M (affineGroupoid (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n)))] :
    eulerCharacteristic M = 0 := by
  sorry

end ChernsConjectureAffineGeometry

items: Affine structure is encoded as an atlas condition rather than a connection: `HasGroupoid M (affineGroupoid E)` says every transition map e.symm ≫ₕ e' between atlas charts (and its inverse) agrees, near each point of its domain, with a continuous affine self-map of E. Mathlib has no connections/torsion; the classical equivalence 'flat torsion-free connection on TM ⇔ atlas with locally affine coordinate changes' makes this faithful and automatically excludes Smillie's flat-with-torsion examples. 'Locally affine' (rather than 'restriction of a single affine map') is used because transition-map domains may be disconnected; on each component the two agree.

Continuous affine maps `E →ᴬ[ℝ] E` are used in the pregroupoid so the composition axiom can be proved for a general normed space; the statement instantiates E := EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n), where every affine map is continuous, so nothing is lost.

The model space is `EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n)` (boundaryless), so 'compact' means closed (compact, no boundary). `T2Space M` is added because Mathlib charted spaces are not automatically Hausdorff; second countability is automatic for compact locally Euclidean spaces and is not assumed. Connectedness/orientability are not assumed, matching the table.

Smoothness is not assumed as a separate hypothesis: the file proves (as an API instance) that an affine atlas makes M a smooth manifold `IsManifold 𝓘(ℝ, E) ∞ M`, so adding `[IsManifold (𝓡 n) ∞ M]` would be redundant.

The hypothesis `0 < n` excludes dimension 0, where a single point is a compact affine manifold with χ = 1 and the literal statement is false; every source implicitly assumes positive dimension. The odd-dimensional (trivially true) cases are kept, as the table requires.

Euler characteristic is defined as ∑ᶠ k, (-1)^k · dim_ℚ H_k(X; ℚ) using Mathlib's singular homology with coefficients in ModuleCat ℚ (coefficient module `ULift.{u} ℚ` to keep the definition universe-polymorphic). For compact manifolds all Betti numbers are finite and vanish above the dimension, so the `finsum`/`finrank` defaults (0 on infinite support / infinite dimension) are never reached; rational Betti numbers give the same χ as integral ranks by universal coefficients. A test proves χ(point) = 1.

The bespoke definitions (`bettiNumber`, `eulerCharacteristic`, `affinePregroupoid`, `affineGroupoid`) are generic and would normally live in FormalConjecturesForMathlib; they are placed in the problem file only because the task restricts writing to the single candidate file.
Uses `M : Type*` (universe-polymorphic) rather than `Type` as in the Poincaré file; this is harmless.

reviewer_notes: Ambiguity in the source: 'compact affine manifold' taken literally includes dimension 0, where a point (finite set) is a compact affine manifold with nonzero χ, making the statement false. All candidates except c01 add the hypothesis 0 < n, which I judge to be the universally intended convention (the interesting content is even n ≥ 4; odd n is trivial by Poincaré duality). c01 omitted it and is therefore a provably false statement — rejected on that ground alone. Two equivalent encodings of 'affine structure' appear among candidates: (a) each transition map is globally the restriction of one affine equivalence (c01, c03, c08), (b) transition maps are locally affine, i.e. the (Aff(ℝⁿ),ℝⁿ) groupoid (c02, c04–c07). They define the same class of manifolds (any affine manifold admits a refined atlas with connected chart overlaps, on which locally affine = globally affine), so both are faithful as universally quantified statements; (b) is the textbook definition (Goldman/Thurston) and integrates with Mathlib's HasGroupoid framework, so it was chosen. Bespoke definitions (bettiNumber, eulerCharacteristic, affinePregroupoid, affineGroupoid) are generic and would ideally live in FormalConjecturesForMathlib in a real PR; they are kept in the problem file here per the single-file constraint, with fully proved API/test lemmas (χ(point)=1; affine atlas ⟹ smooth manifold). Mathlib has neither connections on TM nor an Euler characteristic, so the atlas formulation and rational-singular-homology χ are the necessary modeling choices; both are explicitly licensed by the decomposition notes. Final file compiles with only the 'declaration uses sorry' warning.
